pr.title: Gather a drawer's review threads under their files
pr.head: 79394338d0a23765e5f51caa5a8f3650e964a4db

summary: Projector's panel sits above Claude Code's prompt and lists the pull requests a session fixes or reviews. Pressing a pull request's number opens its drawer: a few lines under the pull request that show its branch and size, two actions, links to GitHub and to its Projector summary, and the pull request's unresolved review threads.

Each thread's line used to repeat the full file path and then cut the finding's first line at 60 characters. On a pull request with several findings in one deeply nested file, the path filled most of each line, and the cut removed the words that told the findings apart.

This change names each file once, as a line that counts the file's threads, and indents that file's threads two columns under it. Every file starts collapsed, marked +. Click a file, or press Enter with the focus ring on it, to show its threads and mark it -. A thread's line starts with :<line>, or file for a comment on the whole file, and runs to the panel's edge:

- ios/Field/Audio/TrackPlayer.swift 2*
  :1875 · grace · P2 · One song's failed rebuild blocks other songs from recovering
  :1902 · grace · outdated · P2 · A background rebuild can overwrite a newer imported track
+ docs/notes.md 1*
Threads keep their oldest-first order within a file, and files come in the order of each file's oldest thread. The drawer's other rows do not change.

cards.title: Terms
cards.html:
• Drawer: the lines a pull request's row opens under itself in the panel.
  • Thread label: the text of one thread's link, built by threadLabel.
  • columns: how wide the panel's rows are, the terminal's width less the panel's inset and padding.
  • labelWidth: the width of the column of pull request numbers. The drawer starts one column past it.
  • panelOpenFiles: the session state that holds which files are open, for one drawer at a time.

cards.title: Review so far
cards.html:
• The review of 20aa773 was clean, with one suggestion: move rowOf's doc comment back above rowOf. This head does that.
  • The review of 7939433 requests changes. One finding is open: a closed and reopened drawer keeps the files you opened, while the docs say each drawer opens collapsed.
  • The new tests fail against the previous head's code, and the full gate passes at this head.

groups.title: Threads gathered under collapsible files
groups.kicker: How the drawer groups threads, collapses each file, and cuts each thread's line
intro: threadsByFile groups the drawer's threads by their full path in a Map, which keeps the order in which each path first appears. The threads come from GitHub oldest first, so each file lands where its oldest thread does, and each file's threads stay oldest first.

Each file draws as a plain Button that reads + <path> <n>*, with the count in warning, the same yellow as the * on the pull request's row. The button has no hotkey, so it takes no digit. In the focus ring it comes after Dismiss. A press calls toggleFile, which adds the path to or removes it from panelOpenFiles for that drawer. A press in another drawer starts that drawer's list from empty.

threadLabel builds a thread's text from its line, its author, outdated, and its excerpt, in that order, and cuts it with … at the width it is given. The excerpt comes last so that the cut takes it first. The label falls back to file when the thread has no line, so a comment on a whole file never draws an empty link.

The panel cuts the text itself instead of setting wrap="truncate-end" on the Text. A terminal without hyperlinks draws a link as its text followed by its URL, and a truncating Text would cut that URL off.

files.note: Replaces the 60-character excerpt cut with a cut at the drawer's width, adds threadsByFile and the panelOpenFiles state, and draws each file as a toggle Button with an indented column of thread links under it while the file is open.

checks.text: The width passed here subtracts the same labelWidth + 1 that the drawer's marginLeft uses, and THREAD_INDENT, from the rows' columns. A probe at 120 columns cut a 300-character excerpt to exactly 109 columns, and a label one column short of that stayed whole.

Probe tests showed two index.ts files in different directories in separate groups, 40 interleaved threads across 13 files in 13 groups ordered by each file's first thread, and resolved threads left out of both the list and the count.

A closed and reopened drawer keeps the files you opened, because nothing clears panelOpenFiles when a drawer opens. A probe that opened src/a.ts, then closed and reopened the drawer, drew - src/a.ts 1* with its thread showing. docs/plugins.md says every file starts collapsed and stays open only while its drawer does.

files.note: Declares the panelOpenFiles state key: the drawer it belongs to and the paths of its open files.

groups.title: Tests
groups.kicker: The drawer test, and new tests for grouping, collapse, and the width cut
intro: The existing drawer test now expects one file: box per file after the links row. threadsOf opens every collapsed file first, then reads each file's threads' link targets and text, and checks that each thread sits two columns in and leaves its Text free to wrap. fileLinesOf reads each file's toggle button.

New tests use drawerListing, which opens x/y#7's drawer over a list of threads you give it. They pin the grouping and the file label, the boundary of the width cut, the collapse and expand of each file, an open file that stays open through a poll, and another pull request's drawer that starts collapsed.

checks.text: With 20aa773's hooks/register.tsx and hooks/types.d.ts, the two collapse tests fail and the other 223 pass.

groups.title: Documentation
intro: docs/plugins.md now describes a line for each file that counts its threads and starts collapsed, how a click or Enter shows and hides the threads, the order of files and threads, and the parts of a thread's line. It also says that a terminal without hyperlinks draws the thread's URL after the text.
